text:
priya: Quick sync - we need a pragmatic plan for enrichment ordering for trace cost attribution. Customers ask for near-exact per-request cost while we keep edge latency tight.

sam: Short summary: pre-enrich = accurate attribution at edge but adds CPU/latency there. late-enrich = cheap edge path, pushes work to backend and complicates sampled traces.

liam: Important question: are we resolving simple billing tags (org_id, env) or full billingKey resolution that may require lookups into tenant metadata?

priya: Full billingKey preferred. Accuracy target: <5% per-tenant drift over weekly windows. Latency targets unchanged: p95 edge <= 120ms.

anna: My vote: tiered routing. Mark critical routes (dedicated customers, payments, billing) to always do synchronous pre-enrich. Everything else goes through best-effort late-enrich.

maria: Agreed. For late-enrich we should use micro-batching to amortize lookups. 200-300ms batch window seems reasonable to start.

sam: Caveat: batching increases attribution lag and potentially retry complexity if lookups fail. Also beware of duplicate events when we replay.

priya: Draft proposal: add header X-Attr-Priority: high | standard. If high -> block on local enrichment. If standard -> emit minimal envelope and enqueue for late enrich.

liam: How do we prevent lost keys for sampled traces? If tracer samples away payloads we might not have enough context. Need a fallback lookup API keyed by request_id.

anna: We can propagate a compact request fingerprint from the edge (req_fingerprint) so late-enrich can do a cold lookup. But lookup QPS could be huge without caching.

maria: Implement a small in-memory LRU in the enrichment layer: req_fingerprint -> billingKey, ttl=30s. Hot requests will be served locally. For misses, fall back to lookup-service with strict tenant scoping.

sam: I'll simulate numbers: miss rate vs TTL vs cache memory at 30s TTL to estimate lookup QPS and CPU. ETA: tomorrow EOD.

priya: Operational notes: Console should show an enrichment_lag metric per route and per-tenant. Alert if lag > 1s for more than 5m. Rollout plan must include feature flag and gradual traffic ramp for pre-enrich tagging.

liam: Header example to include in spec:
```
X-Attr-Priority: high
X-Req-Fingerprint: rf-0a1b2c
X-Provenance: edge-v2
X-Tenant-Id: t-123
```
Never allow cross-tenant lookup; lookup-service must validate tenant header.

anna: Security: billingKey persisted only hashed, access audited, and TTLed in caches. Private deployments get an extra compliance checklist and HSM/KMS integration notes.

maria: Also, metrics: enrichment_lag_seconds histogram, enrichment_batch_size, enrichment_cache_hit_rate, enrichment_lookup_errors. Expose per-tenant missed_attributions gauge so we can quantify accuracy impact.

sam: Implementation tasks: 1) sim + numbers, 2) cache shim + metrics, 3) attr-priority header opt-in, 4) lookup-service fallback with tenant guardrails.

priya: Owners: Sam -> sims and telemetry, Liam -> header & lookup API spec, Anna -> obs-gateway routing changes, Maria -> cache design and security checklist. I'll own rollout coordination and Console knobs.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-8420 for enrichment routing prototype and monitoring. https://tasks/redwood/INFRA-8420

priya: OK. If someone prototypes and hits a perf wall, call it out immediately. We'll keep the default as late-enrich for low-impact routes to avoid regressing latency.

liam: One operational tip: please include a small chaos test during canary that drops enrichment lookups to measure attribution degradation.

anna: +1. I'll add a canary test plan.

maria: Will draft the cache eviction policy and memory budget tomorrow.

sam: I'll post the simulation results in this thread when ready.

priya: Thanks all. Meeting follow-up: we'll reconvene next Tues to review sims and a first-cut spec.
